query: What signals suggest an incident resolution will be inefficient?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Resolution duration is a core measure of resolution efficiency and gives a genuine continuous axis to model on. Derivable from opened_at/closed_at timestamps present in the table; sample values are plausible durations.

per_column.name: hours_to_last_update
per_column.rationale: Derivable from timestamps, but its value distribution is identical to resolution_hours (same top-value multiset, and in samples closed_at equals sys_updated_on so both equal the same number). It is effectively a duplicate of resolution_hours here, adding little new leverage.

per_column.name: assignee_changed
per_column.rationale: Reassignment is a strong, non-trivial signal of inefficient resolution. However the table has only a single assigned_to snapshot with no history, so a per-row 'assignee changed' flag cannot be soundly derived; the 1/0 values appear inferred without supporting evidence.

per_column.name: is_high_priority
per_column.rationale: A binary derived from the existing priority column; grounded and warranted. Somewhat redundant with the original priority field and near-constant (421/79), which limits added leverage, but priority is a plausible efficiency signal.

per_column.name: inefficiency_score
per_column.rationale: A composite index directly targeting the query is analytically useful for ranking/grouping. But it inherits the ungrounded assignee_changed input and its weighting is opaque; the scores partly rest on unsupported components, weakening groundedness.

judge.rationale: The set provides genuinely useful efficiency axes (duration, priority flag, composite score) for the query. Weaknesses: hours_to_last_update duplicates resolution_hours, and assignee_changed (plus the inefficiency_score that depends on it) asserts a reassignment signal the single-snapshot table cannot support, indicating hallucinated per-row values. Grounded columns (durations, priority) are sound readings of present timestamp/priority data.
